title: Paris as headquarters; musicians knew everything about him
summary: Based in Paris, Moore found French musicians knew his recordings and career in detail.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, how did you like Paris? And did you...

I loved it. That was our headquarters. I don't care where we go. If it wasn't too far, say about... He'd do things around there... I think it was 300 kilometers, which is the miles in France, from Paris, France, to Belgium, Barcelona, Spain... Yeah, that was probably 300 miles, 300 kilometers. And he'd do... Some places, say, about 50 miles or so out, we'd come back to keep our room right in the hotel...
Did you get a chance to meet any of the musicians over there, the drummers especially, talk with them?

No. I met a few of them, not too many. Some good musicians over there. The thing about France, before you'd come over there, musicians, they'd know about you, they'd read about you, got every record you ever made. They can tell you things you...I forget... They'd tell me what date I made 'em, and who I made them with, who else I was playing with in New York -- they knew everything about me. When you got over here, they'd know... How they got the information, I don't know. But they'd know about you, how long you'd been playing, where you're from, who you worked with -- everything. They'd tell you.
Did that shock you, the fact that they knew so much about you...?

Well, they made me feel real happy. I knew I was going over there with no name, didn't have no name, didn't know nothin' about me, they'd never heard of me, I'm going down there to try to work and knock their brains out... I didn't have to do all that. They knew about me. They knew my material and how I worked and everything. All
I got to is go on over there and back my name up, that's all. Every place I go... I ain't no (?), but whatever it is I do, the people like it, you know.
I think I've been working practically all my life.
Well, certainly you have been for quite a helluva time.
